title: Sebastian and the Drop
premise: Orsen Lockridge, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a calendar invitation from her handler, dead for three weeks, scheduling a meeting at a decommissioned drop site. The invitation is bait, but whose? As Orsen follows the trail through Vienna's gray markets, she learns her handler discovered that the Office's director has been selling the identities of its own assets to a rival syndicate, and that Orsen's own file is next. Hunted by both sides and betrayed by the colleague she trusted most, she must decide whether to trade the one secret worth killing for—the location of the Office's true archive—to save herself, or expose it and burn every ghost she's ever protected. In the end she trades it, but only after copying everything: the meeting ends with the director dead, the archive in play, and Orsen finally visible—alive, named, and dangerous.
about_author: Sebastian Halloran spent a decade working logistics contracts across Central Europe before turning to fiction, drawing on the bureaucratic shadows he claims never to have seen. He lives under no particular circumstances in a city he declines to name.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Three weeks after burying handler Marcus Vane, Orsen receives a calendar invite from his account for tomorrow, 0400, at the old Kahlenberg drop. She verifies it isn't phishing, then can't stop verifying. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread—the dead don't schedule meetings unless someone wants them to.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. She briefs herself on Vane's last case files and finds his final expense report altered—someone inside the Office edited history. Deputy Director Ilse Brandt summons her, all warmth and warning, asking what Vane left behind. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your own institution may be the threat.

chapters.title: Kahlenberg, 0400
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. At the drop she finds no body, but a dead-drop cache Vane prepared before dying: a burner phone with one contact labeled 'TOMORROW' and half a cipher key. A watcher on the ridge photographs her; she lets him. Emotional beat: cold clarity—she chooses to be seen.

chapters.title: The Second Set of Books
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Reiner, Orsen's longtime partner fixer, running a routine extraction that goes wrong when their exfil route is pre-empted by men with Meridian-grade credentials. He covers Orsen's absence without asking why. Emotional beat: loyalty as reflex, and the first hairline crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Cipher
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Decoding Vane's key against an old shared cipher, she recovers fragments: names of assets, dates, and the word ARCHIVE repeated like a heartbeat. One name is hers, flagged TRANSFERABLE. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—she is inventory.

chapters.title: Coffee with Ilse
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Brandt offers Orsen Vane's desk and a clean slate, probing gently about the Kahlenberg trip. Orsen lies well and hates how easily Brandt accepts it—as if acceptance were also a test. Emotional beat: power's soft voice; corruption wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Ordered to surveil Orsen 'for her protection,' Tomas discovers the surveillance order predates Vane's death. He sits on it, tells no one, and starts his own quiet audit. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its war inside him.

chapters.title: The Broker in the Garden
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. She meets Anselm Roth, a freelance intelligence broker who once bought from Vane. Roth confirms a buyer has been purchasing Meridian asset files—and offers to name the seller for a price Orsen can't pay yet. Emotional beat: temptation; every door out costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Laying out evidence in a safehouse, she reconstructs Vane's last week: he found the leak, copied something, and died within forty hours. The math says insider. The method says Brandt—or whoever Brandt answers to. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Tomas Found
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. His audit uncovers a shell company feeding Meridian funds offshore, signed off by Director Aldous Wren himself—the man officially retired two years ago but still in the building. He sends Orsen one word: WREN. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty becomes complicity if unspoken.

chapters.title: Transferable
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Her own file activates: accounts frozen, cover legends burned, a termination order drafted under another officer's signature—Tomas's. Someone is framing them against each other. Emotional beat: betrayal engineered so precisely it feels intimate.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Danube
chapters.summary: POV alternating Orsen/Tomas. They meet armed, each believing the other signed the order, and talk their way back from the trigger. Pooling evidence, they see the design: the Office eats its own and bills the family. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt in the worst possible place.

chapters.title: Roth's Price
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Roth names his fee: the location of the Meridian archive, the Office's master vault of legends, ledgers, and leverage. He reveals the buyer of the asset files is the Karst Syndicate—and that Wren has been selling to fund his own exit. Emotional beat: the secret worth killing for finally has a shape.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Retire
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas tails Wren to a private clinic where the 'retired' director receives dialysis and visitors from Karst. Photographs confirm everything. Then Tomas realizes he was allowed to follow. Emotional beat: triumph flipping instantly to trap-sprung panic.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Both are now formally rogue; safehouses close, contacts go silent, and Brandt leaves a message: come in, give up Vane's cache, and live. Orsen hears the offer for what it is—a countdown. Emotional beat: the price of survival rising past what she thought she had.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Following a mnemonic Vane drilled into her years ago, she locates his real cache hidden in plain sight: a full copy of the transfer ledger and the archive's access protocol. Reading his notes, she hears his voice again. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. She offers Roth the archive location; he delivers Karst's operational plan—they intend to hit the vault during a scheduled 'audit' in four days, killing everyone inside, including the staff who know nothing. Emotional beat: guilt arriving on schedule; the trade saves her and damns others.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Planning the impossible: warn the archive staff, expose Wren, and survive Brandt's internal hunters—all with two people and a stolen credential set. They recruit a disaffected comms officer, Petra. Emotional beat: fragile hope built from borrowed parts.

chapters.title: Storming the Quiet Floor
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Inside Meridian headquarters during the audit, they trigger the alarm early, emptying the vault floor before Karst's team arrives—and confront Wren in the archive anteroom. He offers her partnership with the calm of a man who has never been refused. Emotional beat: power's final seduction, face to face.

chapters.title: The Meeting That Was Always Scheduled
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Climax. Karst breaches; in the chaos Wren tries to erase the ledger and Orsen kills him with the same efficiency the Office taught her. Brandt arrives—not to arrest her, but to negotiate. Orsen gives Brandt the archive location as promised, having already moved the contents. Emotional beat: the trade completed, hollow and necessary.

chapters.title: Everything Copied
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Aftermath: Karst broken, Wren posthumously blamed, Brandt installed as director owing Orsen a debt she'll collect slowly. Tomas burns his own file and walks. Emotional beat: survival achieved at the cost of the institution that defined them.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Epilogue. From a rented room in Trieste, Orsen uploads the full ledger—every sold asset, every ghost—to journalists, embassies, and the families of the traded. She signs it with her real name, the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety; visibility as both ending and beginning.
